part_title: KMS Material Origins and CloudHSM TLS

scenes.title: KMS key-material origin and custody
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains kms key-material origin and custody by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

The first panel compares customer managed KMS keys with AWS-generated or imported key material; imported material needs explicit expiry, reimport and recovery planning. The second panel shows a KMS custom key store backed by customer-operated CloudHSM, keeping KMS APIs but depending on HSM health and capacity. The third panel uses an external key store proxy and an outside key manager, introducing cross-boundary cryptographic operations, latency and outages. These choices alter material provenance and execution locations without automatically changing who administers the KMS key policy.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Key ownership, origin of key material and cryptographic execution location are distinct questions.

scenes.narration: This slide explains kms key-material origin and custody through the actual architecture shown. The first panel compares customer managed KMS keys with AWS-generated or imported key material; imported material needs explicit expiry, reimport and recovery planning. The second panel shows a KMS custom key store backed by customer-operated CloudHSM, keeping KMS APIs but depending on HSM health and capacity. The third panel uses an external key store proxy and an outside key manager, introducing cross-boundary cryptographic operations, latency and outages. These choices alter material provenance and execution locations without automatically changing who administers the KMS key policy. Key ownership, origin of key material and cryptographic execution location are distinct questions. When deciding what architecture to implement, first identify the caller, resource owner and trust boundary. Check how AWS policy authorization, service configuration and operational recovery interact instead of assuming a single setting makes everything secure. The diagram is a decision aid: follow its arrows from the original actor to the final action, and verify each dependency in the running environment.

scenes.title: CloudHSM-backed TLS at the application
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains cloudhsm-backed tls at the application by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

The top-left path terminates TLS at an Application Load Balancer using its configured certificate. The lower path terminates TLS at an EC2 web server which integrates supported CloudHSM client and provider libraries to use HSM-backed private-key operations. The ALB path does not transparently call a customer's CloudHSM for private-key operations. On the right, the prerequisites include HSM cluster availability, private connectivity, compatible client libraries, server certificate deployment and application recovery. CloudHSM is not itself a network traffic proxy.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Locate TLS termination and private-key custody before selecting ALB or HSM-backed server termination.
